name: Kashmiri

ancestors.notes: Indo-Aryan — Kashmiri is conventionally grouped here as the Dardic subgroup (Glottolog; Wali & Koul 1997), though its Indo-Iranian position is debated in the literature.

notes: Kashmiri (کٲشُر, कॉशुर), a Dardic (Northwestern Indo-Aryan) language, ~7 million speakers, official/scheduled language of Jammu & Kashmir (India) and taught/published in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir; the Eighth Schedule (Indian Constitution) scheduled language. Written in BOTH Perso-Arabic (the majority script, standardised by the J&K Academy of Art, Culture & Languages) and Devanagari (used mainly by Kashmiri Pandits); this spec covers PERSO-ARABIC. GRAPHEME KEYS: the consonant inventory is the familiar Urdu/Persian Perso-Arabic set plus the SAME three retroflex letters Urdu/Balochi/Sindhi add (ٹ ڈ ڑ), plus ؠ (U+0620, 'Kashmiri yeh', a letter this script alone uses; maps to the palatalisation diacritic ʲ on the preceding consonant, not a glide -- neither Wali & Koul (1997) nor The Unicode Standard ch. 9 describes this letter by name, so the mapping rests on `kas_arab_broad.tsv` gold alone: of 101 rows containing ؠ, 100 transcribe it as plain Cʲ (نؠ -> nʲ, تھؠ -> t̪ʰʲ, etc., never a fused single segment), and the one exception is the letter's own dictionary-entry NAME rather than a phonetic value of the letter itself). Kashmiri is UNUSUAL among Perso-Arabic-script languages for marking almost every vowel quality explicitly rather than leaving short vowels undotted: beyond the three shared Arabic vowel signs (fatha َ /a/, kasra ِ /i/, damma ُ /u/) it adds five KASHMIRI-SPECIFIC diacritics for vowels the Persian/Urdu inventory has no letter for at all -- hamza-above ٔ /ə/, hamza-below ٕ /ɨ/ (a central vowel with no Urdu/Persian equivalent), the long-alif variant ٲ /əː/, the ring-waw ۄ /ɔ/ and the wavy-hamza-below ٟ /ɨː/ (Wali & Koul 1997; Wikipedia 'Kashmiri alphabet'). Aspirated stops (تھ ٹھ پھ کھ چھ) earn their multigraph keys the same way Urdu's do: one phonological segment, not a cluster (AGENTS.md test 2). أ (U+0623, alef with hamza above) earns its own grapheme key rather than falling through to its component letters. U+0623 is canonically ALEF + U+0654 ARABIC HAMZA ABOVE, and The Unicode Standard, ch. 9 'Middle East-I: Modern and Liturgical Scripts', section on hamza, states the value directly: "when such a hamza is used to indicate an actual glottal stop, the /je/ sound used in Persian and Urdu for ezafe, or the short vowels /ə/ and /ɨ/ in Kashmiri, it should be represented with a separate combining mark, either U+0654 ARABIC HAMZA ABOVE or U+0655 ARABIC HAMZA BELOW" (https://unicode.org/versions/Unicode16.0.0/core-spec/chapter-9/). So in Kashmiri the hamza-above IS the short vowel ə and the alef is only its carrier; reading the sequence as alef's aː PLUS the diacritic's ə double-counts the vowel, which is what produced a spurious aː on 82 of the 683 scored words. Word-initial او is read oː, and this one is NOT sourced: no reference grammar or standard consulted for this spec states the value, and the encyclopaedia table that does is a reading path rather than a citable source. It rests on the gold's own evidence (اوش -> 'oː ʃ') plus the structural point that a bare wāw needs a preceding alif to carry a vowel at all. It is confined to a `positional_graphemes` `word_initial` override rather than a plain grapheme key because an unconditional او=oː key made the row WORSE (PER 0.3231 -> 0.3245): elsewhere in the word the ا+و sequence keeps reading as alif's aː plus wāw's glide w. Replace this with a cited value when a Kashmiri-orthography monograph is in hand. Both values match `kas_arab_broad.tsv` gold (e.g. أدٕر 'ə d ɨ r', اوش 'oː ʃ'). KNOWN GAP, documented rather than silently resolved: Kashmiri Unicode text in the wild is NOT diacritic-encoding-standardised -- fonts/keyboards disagree on codepoints for the same phonetic vowel, and this spec's mapping for ۆ (U+06C6, tentatively /oː/), ٗ (U+0657, tentatively /uː/), ٚ (U+065A) and ٛ (U+065B, both tentatively variants of /ɨ(ː)/) is a best-effort reading of the WikiPron gold's actual character distribution (`kas_arab_broad.tsv`), not yet cross-checked letter-by-letter against a dedicated Kashmiri-orthography monograph; a future pass should replace the tentative four with a cited disambiguation. STRESS: Wali & Koul (1997) describe Kashmiri stress as predictable from syllable weight and not distinguishing lexical items; left unencoded here, a documented exemption rather than an omission. SMOKE CHECKS against `kas_arab_broad.tsv` (WikiPron, Wiktionary-scraped): آب /aːb/ 'water'-like item -> gold 'aː b' (spec: آ=aː, ب=b, matches); آزاد -> gold 'aː z aː d' (آ=aː, ز=z, ا=aː, د=d, matches); آسُن -> gold 'aː s u n' (آ=aː, س=s, ُ=u, ن=n, matches). TIER: `research` -- sourced (Wali & Koul 1997; PHOIBLE-class attested inventory), stress exemption documented, and `kas_arab_broad.tsv` (751 rows, WikiPron/Wiktionary scrape, `crowd-scraped` provenance, registered below) is scored in `scripts/benchmark.py` with a PER recorded in `benchmarks/results.json`.
